_README: Adjudicated QA verdicts, so a reviewed episode stays reviewed.
qa_check.py regenerates QA_CHECKLIST.md from scratch on every run, which means
its checkboxes cannot hold review state -- tick one and the next run erases it.
Without this file, every session re-discovers and re-investigates the same
already-adjudicated episodes. That is what kept the flagged count stuck at
14-16 while real work was being done.
Keys are episode slugs. Under each, a signature name maps to a verdict.
Signature names match the `signature` argument in qa_check.py's issue() calls:
wall-of-text, drift, content-loss, duplicates, backward-jump, truncated,
coverage, round-timestamps, weak-model, language, split-timestamp,
leaked-reasoning, repetition-loop, short-loop, missing-file
verdict: "benign" moves the issue out of the flagged list into a separate
'Reviewed, judged benign' section. Any other verdict (or no entry) leaves it
flagged. Always record a reason and a date -- a suppression with no rationale
is worse than no suppression.
Re-flag by deleting the entry. If an episode is reprocessed and its content
changes, delete its entries so the new output gets judged fresh.
WITHDRAWN 2026-08-28 -- the wall-of-text waivers on ep41/ep43/ep44/ep58, and ep44's
coverage waiver. All rested on one claim: 'the giant block carries a single speaker
label, so it is one real long monologue.' That is circular. A collapsed diarization
cluster produces exactly one label across the whole block, so the label count cannot
witness its own correctness. Reading those blocks found real co-host turns inside
them (ep58 'Devil's advocate sikit, YB'; ep43 'Kau rakyat jelata biasa?' answered by
'Saya rakyat jelita biasa lah'). The size trigger now lives in the separate
'oversized-block' signature, which does not consult the label count.
Waiving an issue needs evidence INDEPENDENT of the artefact under suspicion. Audio,
or dialogue content, or the roster -- not the label whose correctness is the question.

drift.reason: Isolated false phrase-lock, not mistiming. 10 of ep17's 11 matched samples sit within -21s; the single -958s outlier is a 124-char block whose head words score equally badly at the claimed and matched positions (2/10 both), so the match barely cleared MIN_MATCHING_WORDS and locked onto a coincidence. Block [7323s] independently maps to audio at 7441s (p10 7341, p90 7535) by 4-gram origin mapping, and the caption coverage map shows no near-zero run anywhere in the episode. See ENGINEERING_LOG.md 1.23.

Isolated false phrase-lock, same as ep17. Only 3 of 12 samples match at all because ep21's YouTube captions run at about half normal word density (8,182 caption words over 9,574s), which is also why check_caption_coverage.py reports it inconclusive. Two of the three matched samples are tight (-33s, -36s); the +976s outlier is contradicted by 4-gram origin mapping, which puts block [7574] at audio 7596-7669s (correctly positioned) and its neighbour [7832] at 7841s. See ENGINEERING_LOG.md 1.23.

oversized-block.reason: Genuine Rafizi monologue. TWO independent lines of evidence, neither of them the block's own label -- that was the circular error withdrawn on 2026-08-28. (1) Content: the 22.6-min block at [1:46:50] contains ZERO co-host markers across all of it. The four signatures present in every confirmed-mixed block are absent: no run-sheet clock reading ("2 jam 40 minit"), no segment hand-off, no question addressed to YB, no second-person address. It reads as sustained first-person self-defence, opening "naya lah semua menteri dituduh salah guna kuasa" and closing "ini doa akulah kan. Aku tak nak mati". WITHDRAWN 2026-08-28 (line 2 only): the acoustic half of this waiver used to say "pyannote re-ran with an exact speaker count and left this block whole". That is no longer evidence of anything -- setting num_speakers makes pyannote IGNORE clustering.threshold and solve for the cut height instead, so declining to split under a count hint says nothing about whether the block is one voice (ENGINEERING_LOG 1.36). The waiver now rests on content alone. Re-flag by deleting this entry if the episode is ever re-transcribed. Re-tested 2026-08-28 with scripts/cohost_candidates.py, which locates YB vocatives and run-sheet phrases by caption word-timing rather than by reading the block: this block returns ONE hit, "seterusnya dia menjadi perdana menteri", where seterusnya is an ordinary adverb and not a hand-off -- a false positive. Compare ep47, whose two same-length blocks return 15 and 10 hits and which the video then confirmed collapsed. This episode has exactly ONE block over the threshold, so this waiver covers all of them -- qa_check waives per SIGNATURE, not per block, which is how ep27's waiver for its [1:29:28] block silenced a second 21-minute block at [43:51] that the video then showed holds a co-host.

unlabelled-host.reason: The flag's premise is that the person's turns are sitting inside another speaker's blocks. Here there is no evidence he SPOKE at all, so there are no turns to recover. He stays on hosts: because that field records who took part, not who holds a label (scripts/rebuild_roster.py). Evidence, none of it the transcript's own labels: (1) Every textual trace of Farhan in ep39 is THIRD-PERSON, not a hand-off to him. "Ini salah Farhan dan Tim" at [20:38] blames him for a slide, which is his producer role rather than speech, and "apa nama ni Farhan sebut tadi" at 43:57 refers back to something without locating it. (2) Video: frames at both seconds, padded either side, show Rafizi and the guest Iqbal and no Farhan (scripts/frames_at.py, ENGINEERING_LOG 1.35). (3) The caption track's 16,563 word-timings contain no other mention of Pa'an or Farhan to check. Note ep39 lists Iqbal under hosts although the episode introduces him as invited ("kita ada saudara Iqbal. Kenapa kita jemput Iqbal?"); he holds 48 labels of his own and is a separate person from Farhan (Pa'an). A prior note claiming a speaker called "Farhan Iqbal" is wrong -- that string appears nowhere in the corpus.

unsourced-figure.reason: The published files print `200 juta` where raw.md says `700 juta`, for the cost of widening the PLUS highway from Senai to Yong Peng. The caption track settles it: `itu pun dah saya ingat 700 juta`. The old local-ASR raw said `200 juta`, so the rewrite copied a bad raw and regeneration from the MAI raw fixes it.  Note the place name is Yong Peng, Johor: the old raw wrote `Yongping` and the captions `Yompeng`.
unsourced-figure.fixed_2026_09_14: FIXED in all three published files: `200 juta` -> `700 juta`. The owner chose on 2026-09-14 to correct the digits now rather than wait for the regeneration of 33 stale published files, because the repo is public. The replacement is recorded as a reviewed, episode-scoped literal in scripts/fix_published_figures.py with its witnesses, so it is reproducible rather than a hand edit. raw.md was NOT touched: it was already right. A future regeneration overwrites this, which is expected.

oversized-block.reason: Genuine Rafizi monologue: a sustained presentation segment. THREE independent lines of evidence, none of them the block's own label. (1) Content: the 20.3-min block at [35:40] contains ZERO co-host markers across 1,829 words -- no YB vocative, no run-sheet hand-off (scripts/cohost_candidates.py). That is the same signature as ep51's waived block, and the opposite of ep47's two 24-min blocks, which returned 15 and 10 hits and which the video then confirmed collapsed. (2) Acoustic, using the dial that actually works: clustering.threshold=0.55 with no speaker count split THIS EPISODE's other three oversized blocks (49, 39 and 28 min) down to 140 turns and recovered Haziq, who was not even on the roster -- and declined to split this one. The method demonstrably works on this exact audio and still left this block whole. Note this is a stronger claim than the acoustic line withdrawn from ep27/ep36/ep51 on 2026-08-28, which relied on num_speakers; a speaker count makes pyannote IGNORE the threshold, so declining under a count hint meant nothing (ENGINEERING_LOG 1.36). (3) Video: frames at 38:00, 45:00 and 52:00, spread across the block and padded either side, show Rafizi ALONE in a close single shot with his mouth open in all 15 frames, with no cut and a persistent 'KRONOLOGI 40 MUKA SURAT' QR overlay (ENGINEERING_LOG 1.35). Re-flag by deleting this entry if the episode is ever re-transcribed.

unsourced-figure.reason: `1.99` is a notation difference, not a changed figure. raw.md says `seringgit 99 sen` in words and the published text prints `RM1.99`. Same value, and digits are correct newspaper style for the interview files. check_figures.py compares digit strings, so it cannot see a figure spelled out in Malay words. No other figure in the episode is flagged.

duplicate-turn.reason: Not a chunk artefact: raw.md contains BOTH lines, three seconds apart -- `[2:42:13] Rafizi: Malaysia ni untuk Azam Baki aje.` and `[2:42:16] Rafizi: Malaysia ni untuk Azam Baki sahaja.` The speaker restated himself, and interview.md keeps the two wordings distinct. Only interview-en.md looks duplicated, because `aje` and `sahaja` both translate to `only` -- a faithful translation, not a repeated turn.

A translation collapse, not a duplicated turn. interview.md carries two DIFFERENT lines (`Wah, pengalaman you pun lain sikit juga.` and `Wah, binik pengalaman you pun lain sikit juga.`) and raw.md grounds two separate `pengalaman you` utterances, at [07:24] and later. interview-ms.md renders both with the same wording. The content is sourced; only the Malay rendering loses the distinguishing word.

raw-unnamed-speaker.reason: `Audience` is a SANCTIONED label, named as such in CLAUDE.md rule 9 alongside `Multiple speakers`, and it is not a finding. All 7 turns are audience reaction at a live recording. There is no individual to identify, so the advice this signature prints (video frames, the episode description, voiceprints) does not apply.

generic-label.reason: `Hadirin` is simply `Audience` in Malay, so interview-ms.md is translating a sanctioned label rather than discarding a name. The 4 turns correspond to the same audience reaction as the raw-unnamed-speaker entry above. check_published.py counts it as generic because it compares against raw.md's named speakers and `Audience` is not a person.

unlabelled-host.reason: Farhan holds no SOLO turn in ep19 and correctly so. The owner identified him by ear at [2:24:55], speaking the name 'Mahdzir Khalid' TOGETHER with Rafizi, so the honest label for that turn is `Multiple speakers` -- naming it Farhan would drop Rafizi, and naming it Rafizi would drop Farhan. He is on hosts: via rebuild_roster.PRESENT_UNLABELLED because that field records who took part, not who holds a label. Stronger than the ep39 and ep55 waivers of this same flag, which rest on 'no evidence he spoke at all': here there IS evidence he spoke, and it is already in the transcript under a shared label. Note the structural tension: EVERY PRESENT_UNLABELLED entry trips this check by construction, since one adds a roster name raw.md has no label for and the other flags exactly that.

unsourced-name.reason:
RE-JUDGED 2026-09-15 after ep27 was adopted, because the 2026-08-29 waiver was written against the local-ASR raw and qa_reviewed's own README says to re-judge a reprocessed episode. It now flags TWO names and they are not the same case.

`nurul izzah` IS BENIGN, as before: a legitimate full-name expansion. raw.md says `Izzah` and the published text writes `Nurul Izzah` once then `Izzah` after. Note this only reads correctly again because the corpus-wide `Izah` -> `Izzah` fix landed the same day; MAI had regressed the spelling the local raw already had right.

`zahid hamidi` IS REAL AND IT IS A REWRITE FABRICATION. The published text prints `Oh, Zahid Hamidi pun tak ada?` and NO witness supports it. The pre-adoption local raw said `Zahid Ibrahim`, MAI says `Syed Ibrahim`, and the Malay caption track says only `Oh Ibrahim pun tak ada`. So the rewrite took a garbled first name and resolved it to a DIFFERENT and far more prominent politician, the Deputy Prime Minister, who is not mentioned in the passage at all. That is the ep13 `Lim Guan Eng` class this signature exists to catch.

WHAT IS SETTLED: the surname is Ibrahim, on all three witnesses. WHAT IS NOT: the first name, where no two witnesses agree. The line is a throwaway joke about who is missing from a crowded on-screen graphic during a cabinet-reshuffle segment, so context does not constrain it either. NOT GUESSED, per rule 8. Needs an ear:
  https://youtu.be/W5gI93CKvl0?t=1617
Once the first name is known, correct the published text through scripts/fix_published_figures.py's sibling path or a reviewed entry in fix_proper_nouns.py, depending on whether the raw or the published side is wrong. STAYS FLAGGED until then.

oversized-block.reason: MEASURED, not read. The flag asks for the block to be read before waiving and warns that one label is not proof of one person, so this was answered with the per-block voiceprint test rather than by eye: 26 blocks of the cluster holding this one score mean +0.837 against the Rafizi reference with sd 0.038, and low spread is the tool's own criterion for a single voice. The runner-up is Haziq at +0.619, a gap of 0.218. ep62 is a 3h55m FELDA expose in which Rafizi reads through a white paper page by page, so one speaker legitimately holds 219.1 of 234.5 minutes. Blocks were already re-cut once with reattribute_blocks --threshold=0.55 (53 -> 184 turns, surfacing Haziq and Farhan), so this 20-minute block is what survives a re-cut, not an un-attempted collapse. Pushing the threshold to 0.45 is the wrong trade: on ep58 it took the top cluster to 77% but shattered the co-host across three clusters and made him unnameable.

garbled-agency.reason: THE SPEAKER SAID IT, so raw.md keeps it. `Suruhanjaya Lantikan Kehakiman` is missing the `Pe` of the agency's own `Suruhanjaya Pelantikan Kehakiman` (jac.gov.my), and the same corpus writes the full form in ep03, ep23 and ep37 -- but three independent witnesses all heard the short form here: local ASR (`Suruhanjaya Lantikan Kehakiman, JAC tahun 2009`), MAI (`uh, buat Suruhanjaya Lantikan Kehakiman JAC tahun 2009.` at 1551.4s) and the YouTube caption track (`Suruhanjaya Lantikan Kehakiman GAC tahun 2009`). The speaker's own preceding clause is `itu dalam lantikan hakim`, the same shortening, and he names JAC in the next breath, so the citation is not ambiguous to a reader. Rule 5 keeps a spoken word that carries meaning; rule 2 is about a name the ASR got wrong, and it did not. Not corrected in raw.md or the published files. https://www.jac.gov.my/en/commission/introduction

NOT a garbled ministry name. `Kerana` here is the ordinary Malay conjunction meaning `because`, and the ASR only missed the sentence break before it and capitalised it. The full sentence reads `saya nak kena tanya kabarlah kepada pasukan di Kementerian. Kerana kalau betul mereka boleh melahirkan robot yang boleh buat kerja seperti itu` -- ask the team at the Ministry, BECAUSE if it is true they can produce robots that do that work. Rewriting it to `Kementerian Kewangan` would delete the word `because` and insert a ministry nobody named. The topic is oil-palm harvesting robots and a local factory, so Finance is the wrong ministry anyway; Rafizi held Economy. This is the same class as the `Mas` near-miss already recorded in fix_proper_nouns.py, where 99 hits were places and not the airline. CLAUDE.md rule 2 says read a hit before fixing it, and this is why.

cast.reason: check_cast.py (CLAUDE.md rule 9) reports 60 turns labelled `YB Rafizi` where every other episode says `Rafizi`. It is the same person. NOT PATCHED HERE, on the owner's standing rule of 2026-09-12: an unadopted episode comes up to standard by REPROCESSING it with the camera reference, never by hand-patching its local-ASR raw, because adoption rebuilds raw.md and overwrites any patch. ep08 has no camera reference yet. normalize_speaker_labels.py cannot do it either -- that tool only rewrites the `**Name:**` label in interview*.md, never raw.md's `[time] Name:`. Fix it when ep08 is adopted, by adding `YB Rafizi` to its RENAME map or to data/forced_labels.json.

missing-from-cast.reason: REAL but deliberately not fixed yet. raw.md labels turns `YB Rafizi` where the host is `Rafizi`, so it is one person under two labels and normalize_speaker_labels.py is the tool for it. CLAUDE.md rule 9 already names this case. NOT fixed now because ep08 is unadopted: it still runs on whisper-med and is one of the 36 episodes waiting for a camera reference. Adoption rewrites every label from the camera, so a patch today is wasted work under the owner's standing rule. Re-check after ep08 is adopted; if the variant survives, run normalize_speaker_labels.py --write.

cast.reason: check_cast.py reports raw.md's label `Prof. Barjoyai` against the frontmatter guest `Prof. Emeritus Dr. Barjoyai Bardai`. That is CLAUDE.md rule 3 working as written: the frontmatter carries the full name, the body stays verbatim as spoken. The checker's prefix test cannot see it because the full name inserts `Emeritus Dr.` in the MIDDLE rather than appending to the label. Same person, no defect.

missing-from-cast.reason: A short form of a name already in the cast, not a missing person. raw.md labels turns `Prof. Barjoyai` and guests holds `Prof. Emeritus Dr. Barjoyai Bardai`, the same economist. CLAUDE.md rule 3 is explicit that raw.md stays verbatim as the guest is addressed on air while the frontmatter takes the full name, so both files are already correct. check_cast.py compares strings and cannot see that one is a prefix of the other.

cast.reason:
RESOLVED 2026-09-15, when ep28 was adopted. Iqbal Fatkhi is a HOST in ep28 and a GUEST in ep39 only, which is exactly what rebuild_roster.py already encodes: he is in HOSTS and GUEST_THIS_EPISODE lists ep39 alone. ep28's interview frontmatter carries him under `hosts:` and rebuild_roster reports all 70 episodes already correct, so nothing needed changing.

WHAT SETTLED IT, re-searched on MAI's raw rather than the whisper-med one the 2026-09-13 note used. ep28 itself still says NEITHER: no `jemput`, no `hos`, no `tetamu`, and its YouTube description names no cast. A READING TO AVOID, because I made it before checking: ep10's `hos-hos Sos Cili, Iqbal` does NOT make him a YBM host, and it does not make him a guest either. It names the hosts OF CILISOS, his own show -- ep10's title is `Yang Berhenti Menteri X CiliSos` and Rafizi says `bolehlah jemput Anwar Ibrahim hadir ke Sos Cili`. That line is about his employer, so it is evidence for neither side. ep11 is the line that decides.

Iqbal Fatkhi speaks in ep29 beside the three regular hosts (64 turns in ep28, 44 in ep29) and is filed under `hosts:`. He is genuinely a host in ep10 and ep11, where the episodes say so outright (`hos-hos Sos Cili, Iqbal`, and Iqbal of himself `hos anda untuk malam ni`), and a GUEST in ep39, which also says so outright (`kenapa kita jemput Iqbal`, `dah 3 4 kali dijemput`). ep29 says NEITHER, and its YouTube description names no cast. ep39's `dah 3 4 kali dijemput` implies these were invitations, and an implication is not the bar PRESENT_UNLABELLED and GUEST_THIS_EPISODE use. NOT CHANGED. Both are still on local-ASR raws with no camera reference, so the question returns when they are adopted -- at which point guest_gallery.py's bijection depends on the answer. If he is a guest there, add the tag to rebuild_roster.GUEST_THIS_EPISODE.

MAI and the Malay caption track agree on 7.5 (captions say `7.5 bilion` FOUR times and `75 bilion` never), and the sentence's own arithmetic settles it: the text calls the payment higher than the PM's initial commitment of 4 bilion, which 7.5 exceeds and 75 absurdly overshoots. The old local-ASR raw said `RM75 bilion`, so the rewrite copied a bad raw faithfully; regeneration from the MAI raw fixes it.
